papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Classification of Jhana Advanced Concentrative Absorption Meditation (ACAM-J) using 7T fMRI
papers.abstract: Jhana advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) is related to profound changes in consciousness and cognitive processing, making the study of their neural correlates vital for insights into consciousness and well-being. This study evaluates whether functional MRI-derived regional homogeneity (ReHo) can be used to classify ACAM-J using machine-learning approaches. We collected group-level fMRI data from 20 advanced meditators to train the classifiers, and intensive single-case data from an advanced practitioner performing ACAM-J and control tasks to evaluate generalization. ReHo maps were computed, and features were extracted from predefined brain regions of interest. We trained multiple machine learning classifiers using stratified cross-validation to evaluate whether ReHo patterns distinguish ACAM-J from non-meditative states. Ensemble models achieved 66.82% (p<0.05) accuracy in distinguishing ACAM-J from control conditions. Feature-importance analysis indicated that prefrontal and anterior cingulate areas contributed most to model decisions, aligning with established involvement of these regions in attentional regulation and metacognitive processes. Moreover, moderate agreement reflected in Cohen's kappa supports the feasibility of using machine learning to distinguish ACAM-J from non-meditative states. These findings advocate machine-learning's feasibility in classifying advanced meditation states, future research on neuromodulation and mechanistic models of advanced meditation.

papers.title: Comprehensive Review of Jalandhara Bandha
papers.abstract: Jalandhar Bandha, traditionally described as the “throat lock,” is a key practice in Haṭha Yoga that integrates musculoskeletal, respiratory, and subtle energetic mechanisms. Classical yogic texts such as the Haṭha Yoga Pradipika, Gheraṇḍa Samhita, and Shiva Samhita emphasize its role in regulating Praṇic flow, safeguarding the practitioner during Pranayama, and facilitating meditative absorption. Anatomically, the practice involves flexion of the cervical spine and compression at the throat region, which may influence blood circulation, vagal stimulation, and endocrine function, particularly at the thyroid and parathyroid glands. Contemporary research suggests potential benefits of Jalandhara Bandha in autonomic regulation, stress reduction, respiratory efficiency, and management of thyroid and cardiovascular conditions. However, contraindications include cervical spondylosis, uncontrolled hypertension, glaucoma, and other conditions requiring cautious application. This review integrates scriptural descriptions, anatomical and physiological interpretations, therapeutic potentials, and available research evidence to provide a comprehensive understanding of Jalandhara Bandha. It highlights both the enduring relevance of this yogic technique in modern health care and the need for further clinical validation.

papers.title: Cactus-like architecture for synergistic microwave absorption and thermal management
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT As electronic devices evolve toward miniaturization, integration and diversification, developing composites with thermal management and broadband microwave absorption has become critical for addressing electromagnetic compatibility and heat-dissipation challenges. Inspired by the multilevel thorny structure of a cactus, this study proposes a biomimetic 3D network structure via a ‘direction-decoupling’ design to enhance thermal conductivity and microwave absorption. Boron nitride nanosheets (BNNS) form horizontal thermal pathways, while cobalt-catalysed nitrogen-doped carbon nanotube arrays (Co@NCNTs) are vertically grown in the interlayer for cactus-like heterostructure fillers. Finally, composites are obtained by combining the solid–solid phase-change polyethylene glycol matrix with the directional assembly process. At a mass fraction of 30 wt% for (Co@NCNTs)@BNNS, the composites exhibit the best microwave absorption and thermal conductivity at a thickness of 2.5 mm. The maximum effective absorption bandwidth reaches 6.72 GHz, with in-plane and through-plane thermal conductivity coefficients reaching 2.55 and 0.94 W·m–1·K–1, realizing simultaneous improvements in thermal conductivity and microwave-absorption performance. Moreover, density functional theory analysis confirms the interfacial bonding between Co@NCNTs and BNNS systems and verifies the advantages of a unique electronic structure for microwave absorption between Co- and nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes. This study provides new strategies for integrated thermal–electromagnetic management materials in next-generation high-density electronics.

papers.title: Anionic high-entropy doping engineering for electromagnetic wave absorption
papers.abstract: High-entropy doping (HED) engineering surpasses conventional methods for optimizing atomic configurations and electronic structures, opening new paths for developing advanced electromagnetic wave absorbing (EWA) materials. However, the application of anionic HED engineering to tailor EWA mechanisms remains unexplored. Herein, we employ in situ pyrolysis combined with a three-stage solvent thermal doping procedure to systematically induce anion multibody interactions, thereby facilitating the inheritance and accumulation of beneficial EWA properties. The research shows that anions with various electronegativities precisely balance free charges and create a significant localized charge imbalance, triggering the ‘directional cocktail effect’. This effect induces an optimal dielectric loss mechanism and enhances the EWA performance. With only 7.5 wt% filling, the effective absorption bandwidth and minimum reflection loss are 7.05 GHz and −60 dB, respectively. Overall, we report an anionic HED engineering within thin a graphite framework, which may be conceptually extendable for electromagnetic modulation of other two-dimensional van der Waals EWA materials. This study presents an anionic high-entropy doping strategy, elucidating the intricate charges state regulation to drive dipole polarization-dominated dielectric loss and efficient electromagnetic wave absorption in thin graphite framework.

papers.title: Effects of Moisture Absorption on the Mechanical and Fatigue Properties of Natural Fiber Composites: A Review
papers.abstract: This review critically examines the effects of moisture absorption on the mechanical and fatigue properties of natural fiber composites (NFCs), with a focus on tensile strength, elastic modulus, and long-term durability. Moisture uptake can cause reductions in tensile strength of up to 40% and in elastic modulus by 20–30% depending on fiber type, mass fraction (typically in the range of 30–60%), and surface treatments. The review highlights Ithat while surface modifications (e.g., alkaline and silane treatments) significantly mitigate moisture-induced degradation, their effectiveness is highly sensitive to the processing conditions. Additionally, hybridization strategies and optimized fiber orientations show promise in enhancing fatigue resistance under humid environments. Despite substantial progress, major challenges remain, including the lack of standardized testing protocols and the limited understanding of multiscale aging mechanisms. Future research directions include developing predictive models that couple moisture diffusion and mechanical deterioration, implementing advanced in situ monitoring of damage evolution, and exploring novel bio-based treatments. By addressing these gaps, NFCs can become more reliable and widely adopted as sustainable alternatives in structural applications.

papers.title: A remarkable ruby: Absorption in dense gas, rather than evolved stars, drives the extreme Balmer break of a little red dot at z = 3.5
papers.abstract: The origin of the rest-optical emission of compact, red, high-redshift sources known as little red dots (LRDs) poses a major puzzle. If interpreted as starlight, it would imply that LRDs constitute the densest stellar systems in the Universe. However, alternative models suggest active galactic nuclei (AGN) may instead power the rest-optical continuum. Here, we present JWST/NIRSpec, NIRCam, and MIRI observations from the RUBIES and PRIMER programs of The Cliff: a bright LRD at z = 3.55 with an exceptional Balmer break, twice as strong as that of any high-redshift source previously observed. The spectra also reveal broad hydrogen (Hα FWHM ∼ 1500 km s−1) and He I emission, but no significant metal lines. We demonstrate that massive evolved stellar populations cannot explain the observed spectrum, even when considering unusually steep and strong dust attenuation or reasonable variations in the initial mass function. Moreover, the formally best-fit stellar mass and compact size (M* ∼ 1010.5 M⊙,  re ∼ 40 pc) would imply densities at which near-monthly stellar collisions might lead to significant X-ray emission. We argue that the Balmer break, emission lines, and Hα absorption line are instead most plausibly explained by a black hole star (BH*) scenario, in which dense gas surrounds a powerful ionising source. In contrast to recently proposed BH* models of dust-reddened AGN, we show that spectral fits in the rest UV to near-infrared favour an intrinsically redder continuum over strong dust reddening. This may point to a super-Eddington accreting massive black hole or, possibly, the presence of (super)massive stars in a nuclear star cluster. The Cliff is the clearest evidence to date that at least some LRDs are not ultra-dense massive galaxies, and are instead powered by a central ionising source embedded in dense, absorbing gas.

papers.abstract: The article is devoted to the revision of the conceptual boundaries of empathy in the context of its application in psychological rehabilitation. The study substantiates the need for differentiation between empathy as a background condition of therapeutic contact and as an operationalized mechanism that initiates neuroplastic and regulatory changes. Based on an integrative analysis of foreign and domestic approaches (cognitive-behavioral tradition, neurophenomenology, attachment theory), a three-component model of rehabilitation empathy is reconstructed, including affective contagion, perspective-taking, and regulatory feedback. It is concluded that the integration of empathy into rehabilitation protocols requires not simply a recommendation to «be empathic», but the systematic formation of a meta-skill of empathic responding in the rehabilitant and his environment. Special attention is paid to the psychology of rehabilitation of the empathy mechanism as an independent research field that accumulates data from neuroscience and clinical psychology.

papers.title: Totemic Mediation and Visual Prajñā: How Lotus and Dharma Wheel Motifs Generate Embodied Śūnyatā Experience in the Dunhuang Mogao Caves
papers.abstract: This article argues that lotus and dharma wheel motifs in the Dunhuang Mogao Caves function not merely as decorative symbols but as active visual apparatuses that generate embodied religious experience through a mechanism we term “totemic mediation.” Drawing on Lévi-Strauss’s structuralist reading of totemism, Descola’s ontological framework, Gell’s theory of art as agency, Meyer’s “sensational form,” and Varela’s neurophenomenology, we define totemic mediation as a triadic mechanism encompassing material–spatial arrangement, ontological transformation of experiential states, and value structure generation. We analyze motifs from Mogao Caves 285, 329, and 361 using a five-step analytic framework: formal–visual description, reconstructed embodied viewing, doctrinal identification, mediation mechanism analysis, and evaluative assessment. The analysis demonstrates that the lotus mediates ontologically along a spatial axis, building a vertical channel between the worldly and the divine through ceiling configurations and upward gazes, while the dharma wheel mediates teleologically across the temporal axis, neutralizing linear temporality through rotational dynamics. Together, these motifs constitute “visual prajñā”—a nonconceptual, embodied cognitive effect that bypasses discursive reasoning to enable direct apprehension of śūnyatā (emptiness). This article offers a replicable analytic framework for examining how religious images operate simultaneously as visual apparatuses and ontological mediators.

papers.title: St Thomas’ tactile visionary experiences from a neurophenomenological perspective
papers.abstract: A neurophenomenological perspective postulates the aspects of perception and cognition to understand visionary experiences. St Thomas’ immediate reaction when he heard about other disciples’ visions of Jesus was not to believe it until he put his finger on the wounds of Jesus when crucified, suffered bleeding and died. After a week, his experiences of seeing, hearing and touching Jesus in a locked room after his crucifixion, death and resurrection are investigated here as natural phenomena due to certain neural processes. The neuronal functions are embedded in the constant interaction of bodily movement, reaction and influences of the cultural environment, resulting in kinaesthetic, tactile and visual perceptions. The explanations in neurophenomenology add value to them as natural phenomena. I compare these with hallucinations in cognitivism and synaesthetic perceptions in physiology and psychology, where sensory information through multiple sensory pathways simultaneously brings experiences from more than one sense.

papers.title: Why can't they stop playing? Relative deprivation and problematic Otome game behavior among adult women.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine the associations between relative deprivation and problematic Otome game behavior among adult female players, test the parallel mediating roles of player-character attachment and maladaptive cognition, and examine the separate moderating role of trait mindfulness. METHOD: An online cross-sectional survey was conducted among 433 Chinese adult female Otome gamers recruited through snowball sampling on Xiaohongshu and Weibo. RESULTS: Relative deprivation was positively associated with problematic Otome game behavior, and both player-character attachment and maladaptive cognition showed significant indirect associations. Trait mindfulness was positively correlated with maladaptive cognition (r = 0.417) and problematic Otome game behavior (r = 0.510), whereas negative RD × TM interactions indicated that the positive RD-related associations with player-character attachment, maladaptive cognition, and problematic Otome game behavior became weaker as trait mindfulness increased. CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that problematic Otome game behavior may be associated with both player-character involvement and maladaptive gaming cognition. The mindfulness interactions indicate attenuation of RD-related slopes rather than a generally protective association of higher mindfulness. Given the cross-sectional and non-probability sampling design, causal interpretations should be avoided.

papers.title: Beyond the 'Big Three': Prospective Associations Between Cumulative Lifestyle Protective Factors and Subsequent Adolescent Wellbeing.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Lifestyle factors are increasingly recognized as important correlates of adolescent mental health and wellbeing. However, existing research has largely focused on sleep, nutrition, and physical activity in isolation, with less attention to cumulative multidomain lifestyle protective factors and their prospective associations with subsequent wellbeing beyond prior mental health. METHODS: Data were drawn from 163 adolescents (55.2% female; aged 12-17 years) participating in the Australian Longitudinal Adolescent Brain Study between 2018 and 2025. Lagged generalized estimating equation models examined associations between cumulative lifestyle protective factors and wellbeing at the subsequent assessment after adjustment for prior wellbeing, age, and sex. Two lifestyle protective factor indices were examined: a Base Index comprising nutrition, sleep, and physical activity, and an Extended Index additionally incorporating mindfulness and social connectedness. Outcomes were positive wellbeing measured using the COMPAS-W and low psychological distress measured using the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K10). RESULTS: Lifestyle protective factors commonly co-occurred across behavioral and psychosocial domains. Higher scores on both the Base and Extended lifestyle protective factor indices were associated with greater odds of subsequent positive wellbeing and low psychological distress after adjustment for prior wellbeing, age, and sex. CONCLUSIONS: Cumulative lifestyle protective factors were prospectively associated with subsequent adolescent wellbeing after accounting for prior levels of wellbeing, highlighting multidomain lifestyle protection as a potentially important contributor to mental health across adolescence.

papers.title: The effect of an integrated application-supported mindfulness-based cognitive therapy programme on depression among adolescents with non-suicidal self-injury: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the effectiveness of an integrated, application-supported mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) programme in reducing depressive symptoms among adolescents with non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI). METHODS: An open-label, two-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted in two public secondary schools in Thailand. The schools were randomly allocated to the intervention or usual-care control condition, with eligible participants pair-matched by sex and baseline depressive symptom severity (n = 48 persons/group). The blended school-based and application-supported MBCT programme was evaluated at baseline, 2 weeks post-intervention, and 1-month follow-up using repeated-measures ANOVA. RESULTS: There was a significant time × group interaction, F (1.73, 162.17) = 62.59, p < .001, ηp CONCLUSIONS: The integrated application-supported MBCT programme effectively reduced depressive symptoms among adolescents with NSSI. NSSI was used to define the target population and was not a treatment outcome; therefore, effects on NSSI cannot be interpreted.

papers.title: Supporting children with ADHD and their parents: A scoping review of psychoeducational strategies.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) affects around 6.6% of children worldwide and significantly impacts academic, social, and family functioning. Psychoeducation, providing support for a better understanding with illness, is recommended as a first-line intervention for children and their caregivers, yet its scope remains conceptually broad. A comprehensive overview is needed to clarify psychoeducation supporting children with ADHD and their families. METHODS: Following the PRISMA-ScR method, a systematic search was conducted using PubMed and Web-of-Science in April and May 2025 without date restriction eligible interventions (i) included psychoeducational content combining information and practical adaptive strategies, (ii) targeted parents and/or children with ADHD, and (iii) supported daily management and functioning, including routines (e.g., homework, bedtime, school preparation), organization, emotional regulation, and parent-child interactions. RESULTS: Of 3627 records screened, 70 studies met inclusion criteria, ranging from pilot studies to programs implemented in clinical practice. Interventions targeted parents (43%), both parents and children (37%), or children alone (10%); few included teachers (6%). Approaches were primarily behavioral (33%) or parenting-based (24%), with others grounded in educational (20%), family-centered (12%), or mindfulness (11%) frameworks. Most interventions were delivered in person (83%), while 17% were digital. Despite methodological heterogeneity, findings consistently reported reductions in ADHD symptoms and parenting stress, along with improvements in family relationships. CONCLUSION: Regardless of intervention type, psychoeducational interventions demonstrated positive effects on parental beliefs, and on both parental and child behaviors that facilitate the daily management of ADHD and improving family well-being and quality of life.
